1. Objectives of the Assignment

The primary objective of this assignment is to support the Ministry of Finance and Development Planning in achieving sustainable revenue growth by ensuring the formulation and implementation of effective, data-driven tax policies. The Resident Consultant for Tax Policy Division will provide strategic advisory services and technical expertise to improve the government’s revenue mobilization, fiscal sustainability, and the overall effectiveness of tax policies.

2. Scope of Work

The Resident Consultant for Tax Policy Division will undertake the following key tasks:

  1. Capacity building
    1. Support the ministry develop fit for purpose learning and development needs for the tax and revenue policy teams;
    2. Support the ministry on developing a learning and development strategy/plan to respond to the needs identified above.
    3. Support government implement the learning and development strategy.  
      1. .Technical Assistance
  • Support the Tax Policy Division in analyzing and evaluating existing tax policies

All testable Shop Replaceable Units (SRUs) and Line Replaceable Units (LRUs) must be tested IAW applicable technical orders or Original Equipment Manufacturer Acceptance Test Procedures prior to acceptance by the. Commonly, testing of this type is not available from non­manufacturing sources and acceptance testing at destination would result in additional Government expense with no assurance as to the period of time to accomplish the test or the outcome. Cultural Resources Background The Elbee Village site (32ME408) is a significant, multi-component archeological site, most prominently represented by an occupation dating to 1400-1500 CE. The part of the site with the most evidence for a dwelling was found during compliance work completed in 1978 for installation of the driveway leading to the parking lot and river at the southern end of the site (Ahler et al. 1984; Figure 4). This work was cut short by a construction deadline and not as much of the site was excavated as researchers desired at that time. This southern area was revisited in 2010 by the University of North Dakota (UND), showing that there are many intact deposits remaining. General Summary: The National Black-footed Ferret Conservation Center (the Center) in Carr, Colorado houses approximately 66% of the world’s ex-situ population of endangered black-footed ferrets (Mustela nigripes). The Center’s mission is to maintain a viable assurance population of black-footed ferrets in managed care and to produce healthy kits to support reintroduction efforts to the wild. Black- footed ferrets are reintroduced to select sites in several states each year in an effort to meet recovery goals. The Center houses at least 170-185 breeding ferrets year-round. This number doubles during summer and fall of each year as hundreds of kits are born and more are transferred to the Center from five zoo breeding facilities for veterinary processing and behavioral preconditioning. certifications_partner.text: ===== FILE: files/Attachment_1_-_PWS.pdf ===== PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) Project: Installation and Certification of Phase 1 Hangar Compressed Air and Breathing Air Infrastructure Location: C-130 Hangar, Patrick Space Force Base (PSFB), FL 1.0 Background and Objective The newly constructed single-bay C-130 hangar (33,583 Sq Ft facility) at Patrick SFB requires a centralized compressed air generation system to support general aircraft maintenance hangar, an attached machine shop, fabrication shop, and future paint and blast booths. Note: The Paint Booth and Blast Booth are scheduled for future installation, all rooms are currently ready to receive compressed air. The objective of this contract is to procure, install, connect, commission, and med

ment and Grade D breathing air manifolds up to the designated facility drop points, ensuring the infrastructure is fully operational and certified prior to the arrival of the booths. 2.0 Scope of Work The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, supervision, and quality control necessary to install a complete, functional compressed air and breathing air generation system. The Contractor shall tie the new generation equipment into the new already installed facility distribution piping, install isolation valves at future equipment locations, perform simulated load testing, and support final health and safety certifications. 3.0 Performance Requirements 3.1 Compressed Air Generation Plant • Capacity & Type: The Contractor shall install an oil free Rotary Screw air compressor Variable Speed Drive capable of delivering a sustained 500 to 600 CFM. • Operating Pressure: The system shall maintain a consistent discharge pressure of 125 PSI. • Storage: The Contractor shall provide and install an appropriately sized wet/dry receiver tank system (minimum 600-gallon capacity) to buffer future high-demand surges from concurrent blast booth and paint booth operations. 3.2 Air Treatment (Shop Air) • Drying & Filtration: The Contractor shall install a refrigerate

or shall install an oil free Rotary Screw air compressor Variable Speed Drive capable of delivering a sustained 500 to 600 CFM. • Operating Pressure: The system shall maintain a consistent discharge pressure of 125 PSI. • Storage: The Contractor shall provide and install an appropriately sized wet/dry receiver tank system (minimum 600-gallon capacity) to buffer future high-demand surges from concurrent blast booth and paint booth operations. 3.2 Air Treatment (Shop Air) • Drying & Filtration: The Contractor shall install a refrigerated air-drying system and coalescing/particulate filters capable of treating the full CFM load to meet ISO 8573-1 Class 1-2-1 air quality standards. • Condensate Management (Environmental Compliance): synthetic compressor lubricants and yield an effluent containing 15 ppm or less of total oil and grease 3.3 Breathing Air Purification System (Preparation for Future Booths) • Point-of-Use Manifolds & Stub-Outs: The Contractor shall install dedicated breathing air purification manifolds at the pre-designated facility drop points for the future Paint Booth and Blast Booth. • Termination: Because the booths are not yet installed, the Contractor shall terminate these manifolds with heavy-duty isolation valves and test-port fittings/quick-disc

onnects. • Future Capacity: The manifolds must be sized to support future loads (Blast: 2 users at 15-20 CFM each; Paint: 2 users at 4-15 CFM each) and be compatible with future Vortex cooling tube attachments (device that can be integrated into a supplied-air respirator (SAR) to cool or heat the incoming breathing air). • Filtration & Monitoring: Systems must include multi-stage filtration (particulate, oil, and activated carbon for organics) and feature continuous in-line Carbon Monoxide (CO) monitors equipped with audible and visual alarms set to trigger if CO levels exceed 10 ppm. 3.4 Integration, Simulated Testing, and 45th BEE Certification • System Tie-In: The Contractor shall connect all new generation and purification equipment to the existing facility distribution piping and perform leak testing on all new joints. • Simulated Load Testing: Because the booths are not present to draw air, the Contractor shall conduct a full-load operational test using simulated loads (e.g., utilizing flow- meters, orifice plates, or safe atmospheric venting diffusers). The Contractor must physically demonstrate the compressor plant can sustain the required 500-600 CFM at 125 PSI without system failure or excessive pressure drop. • The contractor shall utilize OSHA-compliant mufflers/
